title: autoscaler-contracts-and-staged-node-rotation-playbook
creator: Asha Khandelwal
description: Design and implement a playbook and runtime contracts between the autoscaler and fleet controller that enable staged node rotations with throughput guarantees. This ticket covers: policy surface for SLO-aware rotations, autoscaler reservation API for short-lived hedges, KV cache prewarm signaling, tenant-aware drain ordering, and observability hooks needed to verify contract adherence.
acceptance_criteria: A stable autoscaler API that can reserve transient throughput hedges (duration + tokens/sec) documented and implemented
Rotation controller can perform multi-stage node replacements without violating per-tenant throughput targets in 95% of simulated traffic bursts
KV cache prewarm handshake exists (signal + warmup window) and reduces cold-start P95 latency by >= 40% in canary tests
Console shows per-rotation contract metrics: reserved capacity, actual served tokens, observed SLO violations, and rollbacks
E2E test harness reproduces drain scenarios and asserts no more than one 5-minute SLO breach per 1000 rotation events
plan: Design API: autoscaler.reserveHedge({duration_s, tokens_per_sec, priority}) and autoscaler.releaseHedge(id)
Extend fleet-controller to accept hedges and schedule node swaps in stage windows with tenant affinity consideration
Implement KV prewarm signal: prewarm.request(node_id, model_variant, expected_prefixes) and confirm when warm
Add metrics and tracing: hedge_request, hedge_granted, hedge_consumed, rotation_stage_start/complete, kv_prewarm_duration
Build simulator for stochastic traffic bursts to validate contract under mixed workloads
Run canary on a small dedicated pool; iterate on timing and defaults
Document playbook and operator runbooks for incidents
risks: Hedge reservations may be overused leading to unnecessarily high tail cost if defaults are too conservative
Complex tenant-aware ordering may interact poorly with existing priority reservations causing starvation for low-priority tenants
KV prewarm API depends on model variant metadata; incomplete metadata could lead to ineffective prewarm
Simulator might not cover certain real-world traffic correlations (e.g., correlated user spikes across tenants)
rollout_steps: Run simulator with staging fleet config to baseline defaults
Deploy fleet-controller changes to a single regional dedicated pool (canary) with low-traffic customers
Observe metrics for 48h, tune hedge sizing and prewarm windows
Gradual ramp to 10% of capacity, then 50%, then 100% across regions
Publish runbook and update console UI to surface rotation-contract telemetry
